  "text": "Mara put the watch beside her shoes. On the far bank, something white moved between the trees and was gone.

“Is there a house over there?”

“There are steps.”

“To a house?”

“I haven't gone up them.”

She turned the stocking. A small brown leaf clung to the heel. She picked it off and laid it on the water, where it stayed against the stone.

“You could come back with me,” she said.

Elias rubbed his knee through his trousers.

“I could walk as far as the gate.”

“You said that last time.”

“Last time you wouldn't stop walking.”

The ferryman sat down. Without his pole upright he looked smaller, an old man resting after work. He took something from a cloth and began to eat.

“I didn't know I was meant to stop.”

Elias looked toward the path behind her. The grass she had bent coming down was lifting again.

“No,” he said. “Neither did I.”

She reached for her shoe and tipped it. A little water darkened the stone.

“At home I keep hearing you in the yard.”

“The latch is loose.”

“I fixed the latch.”

He nodded, as though this were news he had been waiting for.

Mara pulled on the damp stocking. She worked carefully around the hole at the toe, though there was no reason now to keep it from growing.

“Will he take two?”

Elias stood and picked up her other shoe.

“Not today.”

He knelt to hold it steady while she slipped her foot inside. His hands were cold through the leather."
